The Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anil Kumar Jukanti
 I.A.Nos.1 and 2 of 2025
 In/And
 Criminal Petition No.15260 Of 2024
Common Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (for short 'BNSS') by petitioner to quash the proceedings against him in PRC.No.46 of 2020 on the file of XIV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Ranga Reddy District, at Kukatpally.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Mr. M.Hamsa Raj, learned counsel for petitioner, Ms. K.Ashwini Tara Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.2 and Mr. Surepalli Prashanth, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.
Perused the material on record.

3. An FIR No.613 of 2019, dated 21.09.2019, came to be registered in Jagadgirigutta Police Station,
Cyberabad district on the basis of the complaint filed by respondent No.2.

Charge Sheet dated 20.03.2020 came to be filed for JAK, J CRLP_15260_2024 the offences under Sections 376, 506,
417, 420 and 109 of IPC.
4.

It is submitted by learned counsel appearing for petitioner and respondent No.2 that, during pendency of the present Criminal Petition, parties have compromised the matter, I.A.Nos.1 and 2 of 2025 have been filed to record and permit them to compromise the matter to compound the offences.
I.A.Nos.1 and 2 of 2025 are ordered.
5. Today, when the matter is called, both petitioner and respondent No.2 are present in the Court.
6. Learned counsel for petitioner placed on record a marriage certificate issued by the Sub Registrar.

The contents of marriage certificate are as follows:
"I S.R.O, Sri PSVSS VEERABHADRARAO hereby certify that SIKOLU PRUTHVI TEJA and ANNAM JYOTHI appeared before me this 18 day of May, 2025 and that each of them in my presence and in the presence of three witnesses who have signed hereunder, have declared that a ceremony of marriage has been performed between them and that they have been living together as husband and wife since the time of their marriage registered under this Act, the said marriage has this 27 day of June,
JAK, J CRLP_15260_2024 2025 been registered under this Act, having effect as from 29 day of May, 2021."
7.

This Court queried complainant i.e., respondent No.2 with regard to the marriage certificate and whether both of them are living under the same roof as a married couple, respondent No.2 stated that she is working in a private firm at Kukatpally and staying along with petitioner out of her own Seekolu Prudvi Teja vs The State Of Telangana on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80072799/

sentences.text: 8. Considered the entire factual matrix of the case, petitioner and respondent No.2 are present in the Court, they stated that they are living together and requested to close the matter.
This Court is of the opinion that the matter be placed before the Telangana High Court Legal Services Committee for identification of parties and filing of report.

Petitioner and respondent No.2, and their counsels appeared before Secretary, Telangana High Court Legal Services Committee with identity cards on 04.07.2025.
9.

The copies of Identity Cards of the respective counsel are also enclosed herewith.
When asked, both the parties stated that they have willfully and without any coercion entered into Compromise."
10. It is submitted by learned counsel for petitioner that petitioner and respondent No.2 are living together and both are leading a happy married life.
This Court on the last occasion interacted with petitioner and respondent No.2 and both informed this Court that they are living under one roof happily, having got married and wish to live happily.

sentences.text:
It has been held that there are certain offences which overwhelmingly and predominantly bear civil flavour having arisen out of civil, mercantile, commercial, financial, partnership or such like transactions or the offences arising out of matrimony, particularly relating to dowry, etc. or a family dispute, where the wrong is basically to the victim and the offender and the victim have settled all disputes between them amicably, the High Court would be justified in quashing the criminal proceedings, even if the offences have not been made compoundable."
12. Dealing with the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph No.40 held as follows:
"40.

Subsequently, a two-Judge Bench of this Court in Narinder Singh [Narinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (2014) 6 SCC 466 : (2014) 3 SCC (Cri) 54] , after considering the earlier pronouncements of this Court, culled out the position thus : (SCC pp.
482-84, para 29) "29.

entities.text: Narinder Singh [Narinder Singh v. State of Punjab, (2014) 6 SCC 466 : (2014) 3 SCC (Cri) 54]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the aforesaid discussion, we sum up and lay down the following principles by which the High Court would be guided in giving adequate treatment to the settlement between the parties and exercising its power under Section 482 of the Code while accepting the settlement and quashing the proceedings or refusing JAK, J CRLP_15260_2024 to accept the settlement with direction to continue with the criminal proceedings:
29.1.
Power conferred under Section 482 of the Code is to be distinguished from the power which lies in the Court to compound the offences under Section 320 of the Code.

No doubt, under Section 482 of the Code, the High Court has inherent power to quash the criminal proceedings even in those cases which are not compoundable,
where the parties have settled the matter between themselves.
However, this power is to be exercised sparingly and with caution.

29.2. When the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be to secure:
(i) ends of justice, or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
While exercising the power the High Court is to form an opinion on either of the aforesaid two objectives.

3 29.3.

sentences.text: Such a power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involve heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society.

Similarly, for the offences alleged to have been committed under special statute like the Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise between the victim and the offender.

On the other hand, those criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves."
13.

Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court at paragraph No.41 held as follows:
"41.

It could thus be seen that this Court reiterates the position that the criminal cases having overwhelmingly and predominantly civil character, particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family disputes should be quashed when the parties have resolved their entire disputes among themselves."

14. In view of the interaction with both parties and their statements before this Court, this Court is of the opinion that it would be futile to continue the proceedings on the file of XIV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Court.
This Court does not see any reason not to close the proceedings.
The complainant herself has stated in the Court that she is married to petitioner, living with him happily under one roof and wish to live happily.
15. In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in K. Bharthi Devi's case (supra), this Court is inclined to JAK, J CRLP_15260_2024 grant relief as prayed for.

In view of the compromise, this criminal petition stands allowed and the proceedings against petitioner in P.R.C.No.46 of 2020 on the file of XIV Additional Metropolitan Magistrate Court, Ranga Reddy District, are liable to be quashed and hereby quashed.
